subject.title: [Feature]:Support per-agent command lanes for multi-agent deployments

question: What public scheduler/config contract should OpenClaw use for foreground per-agent command lane isolation on shared gateways?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix adds public config and scheduler semantics that must settle lane ownership, aggregate caps, and the request trust boundary before implementation.

options.title: Trusted Per-Agent Lanes
options.body: Add a validated agent/defaults config surface that maps agents or groups to server-owned lanes while keeping a separate aggregate safety cap.

options.title: Unified Scheduler Model
options.body: Defer implementation until foreground, subagent, hook, and workload-specific lanes can share one coordinated scheduler API.

options.title: Document Gateway Isolation
options.body: Keep the current shared main lane and document separate gateway processes as the supported isolation pattern for heavy agents.

recommendation.title: Trusted Per-Agent Lanes
recommendation.body: Add a validated agent/defaults config surface that maps agents or groups to server-owned lanes while keeping a separate aggregate safety cap.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history trail runs through the concurrency resolver and gateway lane setup that define this scheduler/config direction.
